title: Retention SLO matrix & recovery playbook for audit events
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a compact SLO-driven retention matrix for audit events, plus a pragmatic pipeline playbook for indexing, backfills, and failure-mode recovery. It is intended for engineers owning the audit ingestion pipeline, SRE on-call, and compliance reviewers.

Scope / audience:
- Audit events emitted by API layer, RBAC-v2 changes, evidence automation, and SIEM export feeds.
- Not in scope: full application logs (non-audit telemetry).

High-level retention SLO matrix (recommended):
- Tier: Hot (30 days) | Use-case: Low-latency query, console/incident investigation | Storage: SSD-backed index nodes in primary cluster | Retention SLO: 99.9% availability for queries, 30d TTL + 6h grace
- Tier: Warm (31–365 days) | Use-case: forensic investigations, compliance reviews | Storage: compressed indices on rotational SSD/HDD/nearline | Retention SLO: reconstructible on demand within 2h, 365d TTL + legal-hold override
- Tier: Cold (365d–7y) | Use-case: long-term audit, eDiscovery | Storage: object store (S3-compatible), rolled-up indices + raw compressed blobs | Retention SLO: retrieval within 48h, integrity checks on restore
- Tier: Legal Hold | Use-case: paused TTL for specific customer/event sets | Storage: retained copies in object store with immutable flags | Retention SLO: retained until release by compliance

Retention windows should be configurable per-customer (enterprise contracts) and per-sensitivity label (PII / privileged actions). Default policy above applies to public customers.

Indexing strategy notes:
- Early (hot) indexing: stream -> kafka -> es-ingest cluster (hot). Index templates include audit schema v2 fields (actor_id, actor_role, target_resource, action, outcome, request_id, parent_request_id, schema_version, fingerprint).
- Schema versioning: embed schema_version on every event. Ingest pipeline validates known versions and routes unknown versions to quarantine queue for review.
- Partial indexing for large events: store event metadata in index, push full event blob to object store and reference via stable blob_id. This reduces shard amplification.
- Shard lifecycle: daily indices for hot tier with ILM policy: hot -> warm after 30d -> cold snapshot and delete index. Use replica count reduction on warm and cold transitions.

Backfill orchestration (idempotent and safe):
- Backfill source: archived raw blobs or replays from kafka (recreate messages with original timestamps).
- Backfill controller: kubernetes job that claims a work slice (time window + shard set) and writes optimized bulk batches to target index alias-backfill.
- Idempotency: use deterministic doc_id (sha256(request_id + event_offset)) and write_with_op_type=index to replace existing docs. Backfill jobs must track watermark files in object store (backfill-manifests/<job-id>.json).
- Rate limiting: cap backfill throughput to 20% of normal ingest to avoid disturbing production query SLOs.
- Validation: post-backfill validation job compares counts by (day, action, outcome) with archived manifests and emits a diff report.

Failure modes & detection:
- Missing events in hot tier after expected TTL -> causes: ILM misconfigured, failed snapshot, broken lifecycle policy. Detection: daily monitor comparing hot counts vs streaming offsets (kafka). Alert: P2. Remediation: run targeted backfill for missing window and hot-reindex.
- Corrupt snapshot / failed restore -> detection: checksum mismatch during restore job. Alert: P1 if restore fails in warm-to-cold restore path for active compliance case. Remediation: try alternate snapshot copy, escalate to storage-team to repair object store segment.
- Kafka consumer lag -> detection: consumer_lag > threshold (60s) for >5m. Alert: P1. Remediation: scale consumers, check partition ownership. If poison message, move to quarantine-topic and continue.
- Backfill job flakiness / OOM -> detection: failing k8s jobs with retry loops. Alert: P2. Remediation: increase batch size safety, split windows, manual run with increased resources.
- SIEM export failures -> detection: export sink ack rate < 95% over 15m. Alert: P2. Remediation: buffer to object store, retry with exponential backoff; if prolonged, switch to degraded mode and notify SOC.

Runbook snippets (on-call):
- If hot counts drop below expected for last 24h:
  1) Check ingestion consumer status (kafka offsets, lags).
  2) Inspect error topic for schema rejects (common cause after RBAC-v2 rollout).
  3) If rejects present, triage schema_version mismatch; if safe, add a compatibility transform to the ingest lambda and restart consumers.
  4) If gap exists, schedule a backfill for affected windows (use backfill-controller CLI: backfill-cli start --from 2025-02-20T00:00Z --to 2025-02-22T00:00Z --priority high).

- If restore from cold fails during compliance request:
  1) Escalate to storage-team and open JIRA-SEC-restore-urgent with manifest id.
  2) Run checksum verification on all snapshot parts and attempt parallel re-download.
  3) If partial, assemble partial index and tag as incomplete for compliance to triage.

Legal holds and retention overrides:
- Legal hold entries are additive; compliance must create a hold manifest with selectors (customer_id, resource_ids, time windows). The pipeline will apply a hold flag on matching blobs and prevent ILM deletion. Holds are immutable except via explicit compliance approval recorded in Confluence.

SIEM export considerations:
- Exports should be derived from warm/cold snapshots rather than hot to avoid perturbing cluster. Batch exports nightly with per-customer bundles.
- Tokenize PII before export or route to a separate PII-aware SIEM connector.
- Maintain parity between exported schema and SIEM mapping—document mapping in confluence page linked above.

RBAC-v2 impact checklist (ingest owners):
- Ensure actor_role normalization step runs before schema validation. New RBAC change events must include old_role and new_role when possible.
- Add dedicated field action_subject_id to link role-change events to identity graph.

Observability/metrics (minimum):
- ingest_events_total by schema_version, outcome, topic
- consumer_lag_seconds per consumer-group
- hot_index_docs_by_day and hot_index_retention_violations
- backfill_jobs_total, backfill_success_rate, backfill_diff_sum
- snapshot_upload_latency and restore_latency

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical TTL for privileged-admin actions (proposal: extend hot to 90d). Needs legal sign-off.
- Automation for legal hold revocation audit trail (who can release holds?).
- Add simulated longhaul-tests to CI to validate ILM transitions under retention churn.

Appendix: useful commands & locations:
- Backfill controller CLI: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-pipeline/tools/backfill-cli
- Backfill manifest location: s3://redwood-audit/backfill-manifests/
- Hot index alias: audit-events-hot-*
- Checkpointing topic: audit-ingest-checkpoints
- Related tickets: JIRA-SEC-487 (retention policy update), JIRA-ENG-1023 (backfill controller improvements)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive but pragmatic; I expect small changes to TTL numbers after legal and SRE calibration.
- Would like review from SRE (Marcus), compliance (Lena) and infra (Ravi) on restore SLOs and object-store immutability knobs.

Unresolved items for follow-up meeting:
- Schedule for ILM policy rollout to reduce replication on warm/cold (impact analysis).
- Estimated cost delta for extending privileged action hot retention to 90 days.

-- Aisha
